name: New Zealand
tagline: Fiord dawns, glowworm caves, roads made for detours.
overview: New Zealand compresses every landscape you've ever screensavered into two islands you can drive across in a day — and then makes the drive the point. The South Island is the headline act: Milford Sound's mile-high walls sliding out of rain-forest, Queenstown inventing new ways to throw yourself off things, glaciers grinding almost to the beach, and star fields over Lake Tekapo bright enough to read by. The North Island answers with Rotorua's geothermal theatre, Hobbiton's improbably real movie set, and Māori culture woven through everything rather than performed at it. The country runs on trust and small scales — towns of four streets, one-lane bridges, honesty-box fruit stalls — which is exactly its luxury. Indian travellers need the visitor visa filed early, and spring or autumn deliver the postcard without the peak-season campervan convoys. Rent the car; the itinerary is the road.

quickFacts.flightFromIndia: ≈14–17 hrs via Singapore or Australia to Auckland; no non-stops
quickFacts.plug: Type I · 230V — Indian plugs need an adapter
quickFacts.sim: One NZ or Spark tourist SIM ≈₹1,500 for 20GB; coverage thins in fiordland — download offline maps

visa.headline: Visitor visa · online, apply 6–8 weeks ahead
visa.body: Indian passport holders apply online for the visitor visa with financial proof, employment letters and itinerary. Processing times fluctuate seasonally and can stretch past a month before the southern summer, so file early and keep flights refundable until the grant. Transiting Australia needs its own transit visa — many one-stop routes forget this.

weather.summary: Maritime and moody — 'four seasons in one day' is the national forecast. Summers are mild rather than hot, winters snow the alps while the coasts stay green, and Fiordland's 7 metres of annual rain is precisely what keeps a thousand waterfalls running. Pack layers in every month and treat sunshine as a bonus round.
weather.bestTime: December – March, with October–November and April as the quiet-value windows

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.notes: Long light, every trail and sound cruise open, lupins ringing Tekapo — peak everything, including campervan traffic.

seasons.label: Autumn & spring
seasons.notes: Arrowtown's golds or lambing-season greens, thinner crowds, softer rates. April is the photographer's month.

seasons.label: Winter
seasons.notes: Queenstown flips to ski town, Tekapo's skies hit maximum clarity, some alpine passes chain-up or close. Cosy, cheap, quieter.

booking.note: Milford cruises, Hobbiton and glacier helicopters sell out weeks ahead in summer — book the marquee three before flights. November gives summer scenery at shoulder pricing, and rental cars drop by half outside peak.

idealDuration.note: Eight nights does the South Island justice on its own; add three or four for Rotorua and Hobbiton up north. Under a week, pick one island and refuse the ferry temptation.

budget.note: Per person per day with a shared rental car. Adventure add-ons are the swing: a bungy is ₹14,000, Milford overnight cruises ₹25,000+. Supermarket picnics at world-class viewpoints are the national budget hack.

safety.headline: Among the world's safest countries; the weather and the roads are the real briefing
tips: Mountain weather flips in minutes — check MetService before every hike and turn back without shame; rescues here are mostly optimism gone long.
Roads are narrow, winding and slower than maps claim: plan 60 km/h averages, never drive fatigued off a long-haul arrival, and remember keep-left.
One-lane bridges have marked priority — the smaller arrow gives way.
Sandflies at Milford and the West Coast are relentless; repellent is as essential as the camera.
The Nov–Apr sun burns fast under clear southern skies — SPF50 even when cool.
Freedom camping is heavily regulated; use designated sites or apps like CamperMate to avoid instant fines.

goodToKnow: Tipping isn't expected anywhere; prices are final and service is genuine.
Biosecurity is the strictest on earth — declare all food, clean your trekking shoes, and expect beagle inspections; fines are immediate.
A 'tramping track' is a hike; 'jandals' are flip-flops; 'bring a plate' means bring food to share.
Book the Milford road day with slack: the 4-hour drive from Queenstown is the attraction, and avalanche closures happen in winter.
Māori culture is living protocol, not performance — accept a hongi greeting when offered, and don't sit on tables (genuinely offensive).
Indian restaurants exist in every town of size; supermarket labelling makes vegetarian self-catering easy.
Fuel up before remote stretches — the Milford and West Coast roads run 100+ km between stations.
The i-SITE visitor centres in every town are superb — free, honest, and they book everything at list price.

cities.name: Rotorua
cities.blurb: The North Island's geothermal heart — geysers, champagne-coloured hot pools, Māori cultural evenings and redwood canopy walks, all faintly scented with sulphur.

image.alt: The steaming orange rim of the Champagne Pool

cities.name: Auckland
cities.blurb: The harbour-city arrival point spread across 48 volcanoes — Waiheke Island's vineyards a 40-minute ferry, black-sand surf coasts an hour west.

image.alt: Auckland's Sky Tower above a harbour of sails

cities.name: West Coast glaciers
cities.blurb: Franz Josef and Fox glaciers pouring off the Southern Alps toward rainforest — heli-hikes on the ice, mirror mornings at Lake Matheson.

image.alt: Franz Josef Glacier descending its rainforest valley

highlights.name: Milford Sound cruise
highlights.blurb: Mitre Peak rising 1,600 metres straight from dark water, waterfalls on every wall — Fiordland's masterpiece, rain or shine.
highlights.detail: Milford rewards weather either way: sunshine gives the mirror shots, and rain — statistically likelier — multiplies the waterfalls into the hundreds. Cruises run 1.5–2 hours past Stirling and Bowen Falls to the Tasman's mouth, with fur seals hauled out on Seal Rock and dolphins freelancing alongside. Book smaller boats over the big decks, take the first sailing before coach convoys arrive from Queenstown, and treat the drive in — mirror lakes, the Chasm, kea parrots dismantling aerials at the Homer Tunnel queue — as half the day's value. The kayak-and-cruise combos put you at water level where the scale turns properly absurd.

image.alt: A cruise boat dwarfed under Milford Sound's walls

highlights.name: Hobbiton Movie Set
highlights.blurb: Forty-four hobbit holes, real smoking chimneys and a working Green Dragon Inn — the Shire, permanently built into a sheep farm.
highlights.detail: What began as a temporary set outside Matamata was rebuilt in permanent materials for the Hobbit films, and the two-hour guided walk through Bagshot Row to Bag End is a masterclass in movie craft: forced-perspective doors, hand-aged fences, gardens genuinely tended. It ends properly — a complimentary ale or ginger beer at the Green Dragon. Book the first morning tour for soft light and empty lanes in photos, or the Evening Banquet for lantern-lit feasting. Two hours from both Auckland and Rotorua, it slots naturally between them. Non-fans surrender within minutes; the place runs on pure charm.

image.alt: Bag End's green door above the Hobbiton gardens

highlights.name: Queenstown's adventure circuit
highlights.blurb: The town that invented bungy: the original Kawarau leap, canyon swings, jet boats shaving cliff walls at 85 km/h.
highlights.detail: Adventure is Queenstown's civic industry, graded for every nerve level. The icons: Kawarau Bridge's 43-metre bungy (the world's first commercial site, 1988), the Nevis's 134-metre monster with 8.5 seconds of freefall, the Shotover Jet's canyon runs, and tandem skydives over Lake Wakatipu. Book mornings for calmer winds and working cameras; every operator sells the footage you'll absolutely buy. The free-adrenaline alternative: ride the Skyline gondola and luge, then walk down the Tiki Trail. One honest tip — pick one or two headliners rather than ticking everything; prices stack fast and the second bungy teaches nothing new.

image.alt: A jumper mid-leap from Kawarau Bridge

highlights.name: Stargazing at Lake Tekapo
highlights.blurb: A Dark Sky Reserve where the Milky Way arches over turquoise water — telescopes, hot pools, southern constellations.
highlights.detail: The Mackenzie Basin's dry air and lighting controls create some of Earth's clearest night skies, formalised as a Dark Sky Reserve. Guided sessions at the Mt John Observatory or the Dark Sky Project's lakefront base bring telescopes to bear on the Southern Cross, Magellanic Clouds and — in season — the aurora australis flickering on the horizon. The luxurious version: Tekapo Springs' star-gazing float, watching the sky from 38°C water. New-moon weeks are dramatically better; check the calendar before fixing dates. By day, the Church of the Good Shepherd and November–December's lupin bloom fill the same shoreline with the country's most photographed foreground.

image.alt: The Milky Way over Lake Tekapo's church

highlights.name: Waitomo glowworm caves
highlights.blurb: Drift by boat beneath a living galaxy — thousands of glowworms lighting limestone caverns in blue-green constellation.
highlights.detail: The classic tour walks you through the Cathedral chamber's acoustics before the finale: a silent boat glide under ceilings dense with Arachnocampa luminosa, each point of light a hunting larva's lure. It reads as pure planetarium until your eyes adjust and the 'stars' ripple with the current. Photography is banned on the classic route — memory does the archiving. The adventurous upgrade is black-water rafting with the Legendary Black Water Rafting Co.: wetsuits, inner tubes, small waterfalls and the same galaxy overhead. Caves sit three hours south of Auckland and pair perfectly with Hobbiton for the definitive North Island day-chain.

image.alt: Glowworms constellating a dark Waitomo cavern

highlights.name: Aoraki / Mt Cook & the Hooker Valley
highlights.blurb: Three swing bridges to a glacier lake beneath the country's highest peak — the best effort-to-reward walk in the land.
highlights.detail: The Hooker Valley Track is ten flat kilometres return, and no other three hours in New Zealand pays this densely: swing bridges over milky rivers, alpine buttercups, and the finale at Hooker Lake where icebergs calve beneath Aoraki's 3,724-metre summit wall. Start before 8am for still water and parking; wind builds by noon on the bridges. The Tasman Glacier's boat tours float you among bergs on the terminal lake nearby, and heli-hikes land on the ice itself. The village's Hermitage hotel serves the classic peak-framed flat white. Respect the mountain's tapu status — Aoraki is an ancestor in Ngāi Tahu tradition, and summit selfie culture stays below the ice.

image.query: hooker valley track swing bridge mt cook
image.alt: A swing bridge on the Hooker Valley Track before Aoraki

highlights.name: Rotorua's geothermal parks
highlights.blurb: Champagne-coloured pools, the Lady Knox geyser and mud that boils like slow applause — the earth's engine room, doors open.
highlights.detail: Wai-O-Tapu is the palette headline: the Champagne Pool's orange-rimmed steam, the improbably lime Devil's Bath, and Lady Knox erupting on schedule at 10:15 each morning. Te Puia adds the Pōhutu geyser — the southern hemisphere's largest, playing up to 30 metres — alongside the national carving and weaving schools and a kiwi house. Sulphur is the region's cologne; you stop noticing within the hour. Evenings belong to the cultural experiences: a hāngī feast cooked underground and a pōwhiri welcome at Te Pā Tū or Mitai rank among the country's most genuinely moving nights. The free version of the geology: Kuirau Park steams away right in town.

image.alt: Steam rising off Wai-O-Tapu's orange-edged Champagne Pool

highlights.name: Roys Peak, Wānaka
highlights.blurb: The switchback grind to New Zealand's most famous ridgeline photo — Lake Wānaka fanning out 1,200 metres below.
highlights.detail: Six hours return, relentlessly uphill, zero shade — and a summit panorama that made this the country's most Instagrammed track. The famous ledge sits 20 minutes below the true summit; sunrise hikers (headlamps up, dawn at the ledge) get both the light and the shortest photo queue, which in peak summer is a real queue. Carry two litres of water, start cold, and check the track's spring lambing closure (roughly 1 Oct–10 Nov). Down in town, That Wānaka Tree — the lake's lone willow — handles the low-effort photography, and Rhyme x Reason brewery handles the recovery. Isthmus Peak next door offers 80% of the view at half the crowd.

image.alt: The Roys Peak ridgeline above Lake Wānaka

highlights.name: Glacier heli-hike, Franz Josef
highlights.blurb: Helicopter onto living ice — blue caves, seracs and crampon walking two hours from rainforest beaches.
highlights.detail: The West Coast's freak geography drops glaciers from 2,500 metres almost to sea level through temperate rainforest, and since the lower valleys receded, helicopters are the way onto the ice. The heli-hike formula: a snow landing high on Franz Josef or Fox, crampons fitted, then two-plus guided hours weaving through ice caves, arches and meltwater channels that reform weekly. Flights are brutally weather-dependent — build a spare morning locally and take the first slot, which cancels least. Book with the pioneer operators (Franz Josef Glacier Guides, Fox Glacier Guiding). The bad-weather consolation is world-class anyway: Lake Matheson's mirror walk and glowworm dells in the rain.

image.query: franz josef heli hike blue ice
image.alt: Hikers in an electric-blue ice canyon on Franz Josef

highlights.name: Overnight on Doubtful Sound
highlights.blurb: Milford's vaster, emptier sibling — reached by boat-bus-boat, slept aboard, remembered for the engines-off silence.
highlights.detail: Doubtful is three times Milford's length with a fraction of its traffic, and the journey filters the crowd: catamaran across Lake Manapouri, coach over the Wilmot Pass, then your vessel for 21 hours of fiord. The overnight cruises (Real NZ's Fiordland Navigator sets the standard) fold in kayaking off the stern, a swim for the brave, crayfish dinners — and the ritual that names the trip: engines and generators cut in a dead-still arm, letting Fiordland's total silence land on deck. Bottlenose dolphins and Fiordland crested penguins make regular cameos. It costs real money and books out by months; travellers consistently file it under 'worth every rupee'.

image.alt: Mist threading Doubtful Sound's dark ridgelines

trips.title: South Island grand loop
trips.summary: The definitive self-drive: Tekapo's stars and the Hooker Valley, Queenstown's adventure circuit with a Wānaka day, then Fiordland for the Milford cruise. One rental car, the country's five best landscapes, and every night earned by a beautiful road.

image.alt: The lupin-lined road running toward Aoraki/Mt Cook

trips.title: Two-island classic
trips.summary: Hobbiton and Waitomo's glowworms southbound to Rotorua's geysers and a hāngī night, then fly south for Queenstown, Milford and Tekapo stars. Both islands' greatest hits in one arc — the honeymoon-favourite shape of New Zealand.

image.alt: Hobbit holes dotting Hobbiton's green hills

trips.title: Pure adrenaline week
trips.summary: One base, maximum G-force: Nevis bungy, Shotover jet, canyon swing and a Southern Alps skydive, with Roys Peak at dawn and Franz Josef's heli-hike as the day-trip crescendos. For travellers whose holiday photos need waivers.

image.alt: A skydiver over Queenstown's lake-and-range panorama

faqs.q: How early should Indians apply for the NZ visa?
faqs.a: File the online visitor visa 6–8 weeks before travel — processing fluctuates and peaks before the southern summer. Keep flights refundable until the grant, and remember an Australian transit visa if your routing touches Australia.

faqs.q: North Island, South Island, or both?
faqs.a: Under eight nights: South Island only — it carries the scenery headlines. Ten-plus nights: fly into Auckland for Hobbiton, Waitomo and Rotorua, then south for Queenstown and Milford. The inter-island ferry is scenic but eats a day; flying between islands usually wins.

It's the country's best feature — roads are the itinerary. Indians drive on the same side, licences in English work directly, and distances are short but slow. Non-drivers can build the same trip on InterCity buses and day tours, just with less spontaneity.

faqs.q: When do we go for the postcard version?
faqs.a: December–February for full summer; November and April for the same landscapes minus the crowds and campervans (November adds Tekapo's lupins, April adds Arrowtown's gold). Winter is for skiers and stargazers — and the aurora australis, if luck cooperates.

Very. Every town of consequence has an Indian restaurant — a large Indian community keeps standards honest — cafés label clearly, and supermarket self-catering is easy. At a hāngī, vegetarian portions exist; mention it when booking.
